summary.text: Sedimentary structures are all the features in sediments and sedimentary rocks that formed at the moment the sediment was laid down.
Structures such as cross-bedding, graded bedding and ripple marks help geologists tell the original position of rock layers in complex terrain.
They also give clues to the setting where the sediment was deposited, and current ripples can show which way an ancient current flowed.

facts.label: Trace fossils
facts.value: Structures made by living things, such as burrows

facts.label: Antidunes
facts.value: Made by fast, shallow flows with Froude number above 1

items.prompt: You find fossil ripple marks whose crests lean strongly toward one side. What most likely made them?

options.label: Waves washing back and forth on a beach
A current flowing one way, like a river
Raindrops striking soft sand
Mud drying out and shrinking

items.explain: One-way currents such as rivers or desert wind make ripples inclined in the current's direction; back-and-forth waves make ripples that do not lean.

items.prompt: A layer of ancient rock is crisscrossed by mudcracks. What does that tell you about the mud when it formed?

options.label: It was soaked with water, then exposed to air
It was shaken apart by a strong earthquake
It sat under deep water that later froze
It was baked by lava flowing across it

items.explain: Mudcracks form when water-saturated mud is exposed to air, dries, shrinks and cracks.

items.prompt: Water over a flat sandy riverbed slowly speeds up. Once sand begins to move, which form appears before dunes do?

options.label: Antidunes
Mudcracks
Flute casts
Ripples

items.explain: In the lower flow regime the bed goes from flat, to some sediment movement, to ripples, then to larger dunes.

items.prompt: In one rock layer, burrows that reach deep into the sediment are common. What does this suggest about the water above it?

options.label: It was very deep
It was frozen solid
It was fairly shallow
It had dried up completely

items.explain: As deeper burrows become more common, the water tends to be shallower; intricate surface traces point to deeper water.

items.prompt: A rock layer has been tilted on end by mountain building, but it holds old mudcracks with curled edges. How can they help a geologist?

options.label: They show which way was originally up
They show how deep the old sea was
They give the exact age of the layer
They show which way the wind blew

items.explain: Mudcracks curl upwards, so they work as geopetal structures that reveal the original top of a layer.

items.prompt: Blobs of wet sand are found sagging down into the mud layer beneath them. What made them form?

options.label: Worms dragged the sand downward
The upper sediment was denser and slumped
Wind piled the sand into small dunes
The mud below dried and cracked open

items.explain: Load structures form when a denser, wet sediment slumps down on and into a less dense sediment below.
